cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). Now he takes on a new topic: food sacrificed to idols. And he opens with something everybody agrees on: we all have knowledge.

cards.question: Paul puts knowledge and love side by side. Which one does he say builds up?

cards.text: Knowledge puffs up, Paul says, and the one who thinks he knows something doesn't yet know as he ought to. I once KNEW I could grab a hot tray with my bare mustache, and friend, I knew it all the way to the smoke.

cards.question: So if knowing isn't everything, what does Paul say about the one who loves God?

answers.text: That person is known by God
That person is made wise by God
That person is given every answer

cards.text: Okay, BACK to the food. Paul lays out what they know about idols.

cards.question: Paul says an idol is nothing at all in the world, and there is no God but one.

cards.text: Paul says there are many so-called gods and lords, in heaven or on earth. SO-CALLED, friend, like the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with, swearing they still had a little charge left.
But for us, Paul says, there's one God, the Father. All things came from Him, and we exist for Him.

cards.question: Paul names one God, the Father. Who does he name as the one Lord?
Paul says all things came through Jesus Christ, and we exist through Him.

cards.text: Paul's still on the food question, and here comes the catch. Not everyone has this knowledge.

cards.question: Some believers in Corinth are still so used to idols. How do they eat this food?

answers.text: As if it were sacrificed to an idol
As if it were nothing at all
As if it were a holy offering

cards.question: Those believers have a weak conscience. When they eat this food, Paul says their conscience is ___.
Paul says eating food sacrificed to idols brings a person closer to God.

cards.text: Eat it or skip it, Paul says, you're no worse and no better. And I'm telling you this as a stamper who lives on a COOKIE PLANET: food does not get you closer to God.
So the well-informed ones have freedom here, and after years in a junk drawer, believe me, I LOVE freedom. But Paul says be careful.

cards.question: Paul warns the well-informed believers about the weak. What could their freedom become for the weak?

cards.text: Then Paul paints the picture. Someone with a weak conscience walks by and sees you, the well-informed one, eating in an idol's temple.

cards.question: When someone with a weak conscience sees a well-informed believer eating in an idol's temple, what will they be encouraged to do?

cards.text: Here's where it gets heavy. Paul says that weak brother is destroyed by your knowledge.

cards.question: Paul reminds the well-informed believers who that weak brother is. Who is he?
Sinning against your brothers by wounding their weak conscience, Paul says, is sinning against ___.

cards.text: Then Paul turns it on himself. No pointing at anybody else's plate, friend, just his own.

cards.question: Paul says if what he eats causes his brother to stumble, what will he do?

cards.text: That's where we'll set the timer for now. But trust me, friend, Paul is NOT done with this food question.

findings.problem: The setup line says Paul is pointing at no one else's plate, just his own. That rules out the wrong answer 'Explain it to him again' on card 14 before the baker picks, because that answer is about the brother, not Paul's own eating.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 2 by a wide margin. Of its 8 choice cards, 5 are multiple choice, 2 are fill in the blank and only 1 is true or false.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line copies the doc's example almost word for word. The example is 'And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.' The card says 'That's where we'll set the timer for now. But trust me, friend, Paul is NOT done...' Only a few words are swapped.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
